thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Realtime alert: p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1. p99 = 2800ms (SLO 1500ms). Traffic routing shows elevated tail latency and increased timeouts. Alert rule: streaming_p99_realtime_v2.

raj: got the page, I'm oncall. pulling up dashboards now — @emily can you grab infra traces?

emily: on it. grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/streams/stream-latency?orgId=1&from=now-30m
emily: quick read: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~900ms, p99 ~2800ms. error rate up from 0.1% to 1.8% in last 10m.
emily: kube node CPU on eu-west-1-gpu-pool spiking, some pods showing backpressure and steady 120k open connections on streaming-proxy.

maria: we have 7 customer support tickets referencing slow responses and aborted streams (customers mostly EU/Edu and a Level 2 SaaS customer). forwarding ticket ids to @support-ops.

support-ops: impacted customers: org_342, org_998, org_1204. Estimated % of total streaming traffic affected ~12%. logging shows a wave of long context requests (seq len > 12k tokens) around the spike.

dave: can we triage whether this is infra (node/driver) or model runtime? can someone check GPU mem pressure + OOM events?

emily: pulling node logs. saw repeated nv_peer_mem errors on two nodes and one node restarted kworker. no OOMs in containerd but driver logs show multiple failed memcpy calls.

emily: docker logs snippet:
```
E 15:14:02 driver: memcpy failed: rc=-9
W 15:14:05 runtime: kv-cache eviction thrash
E 15:14:07 serve: stream stall: client_wait > 30s
```

zach: model runtime telemetry shows KV cache hit rate dropped from 82% to 10% for a hot prefix; sustained cache misses cause regen and longer GPU work. Could be cache eviction due to memory fragmentation.

raj: immediate mitigation options?

dave: two quick options — 1) route traffic away from the two flaky nodes / scale up pool, 2) flip streaming->nonstream fallback for heavy-context requests (faster path, slightly higher token cost).

maria: customers prefer continued responses even if degraded. recommend non-stream fallback for now.

raj: agree. I'll do a quick routing change to avoid the bad nodes and enable fallback flag for streaming. execute commands below.

raj: routing change (k8s):
```
kubectl patch svc stream-proxy -n eu-west-1 -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"avoid_nodes":"true"}}}'
# or alternatively increase replica count
kubectl scale deployment stream-proxy -n eu-west-1 --replicas=12
```

raj: enable fallback feature flag (console API):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" https://config.redwood.local/api/v1/flags/streaming_fallback -d '{"enabled":true, "scope":"eu-west-1"}'
```

emily: scaling up pool — provisioning new nodes now (requested +3 g4dn-equivalents). watching connection churn.

support-ops: informing impacted customers: message sent to org_342 and org_998: "We're aware of streaming slowness in EU region, temporarily enabling degraded streaming (non-stream fallback) while we stabilize."

zach: note: non-stream fallback increases tail memory churn for very long contexts but avoids the streaming proxy head-of-line stalls. good short-term trade.

15:22 raj: routing change applied, feature flag enabled for eu-west-1.

15:25 emily: new nodes coming up, connection count dropping on old nodes from 120k->32k, p99 trending down to ~1.6s. errors dropping.

15:30 support-ops: customer org_342 reports improved behaviour. tickets updated.

15:34 zach: p95 720ms, p99 1400ms, still above target but within safe range for gradual rollback. tail stalls reduced.

15:40 raj: reduction observed across dashboards, still seeing a small subset of long-context requests doing heavy regen. created a rate-limit rule for >10k token requests for 10m window to protect cluster.

raj: applied temporary rate-limit via gateway:
```
POST /gateway/rate_limit
payload: {"route":"/stream","condition":{"tokens_gt":10000},"limit":5,"window":600}
```

emily: driver team to open a follow-up ticket for nv_peer_mem errors, collecting node dump.

dave: create a post-incident ticket for root-cause: investigate driver memcpy errors, cache eviction policy and autoscaler sizing for streaming-proxy.

raj: summary for incident channel: initial SLO breach detected by alert (p99 spike). cause: GPU driver memcpy errors + KV-cache thrash on hot prefixes causing streaming stalls and proxy head-of-line blocking. mitigations: reroute away from flaky nodes, scale pool + enable non-stream fallback, apply temporary rate limit on huge-context requests. customer impact: ~12% streaming traffic, 3 known customers affected with degraded UX. current status: p99 down to 1400ms, monitoring. oncall handoff to emily in 30m for follow-up. postmortem ticket created: PM-INC-2026-042.

maria: thanks team — I'll draft the customer status email once postmortem has more detail. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Note: This thread will be archived to incidents and a postmortem checklist has been created.
